text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government estimates to spend 24 billion kwacha in conducting presidential and parliamentary elections set for November 18, finance minister Ronald Penza said on Wednesday.

- Crude oil is expected to start flowing into Zambia from the Tanzanian port of Dar-es-Salaam this week, ending a fuel shortage caused by maintenance problems at the port. Energy minister Edith Nawakwi said 270,000 metric tonnes of oil were expected to arrive n the country following the completion of rehabilitation work at the port.
- At least one person was burnt to death in a fire that gutted a market in northern town of Kitwe on Wednesday. Scores of marketeers had their stalls destroyed in the fire.
- The students union has warned politicians to stay off the University of Zambia campus because they are disrupting normal operations there.
- The Zambia Red Cross Society has embarked on a countrywide first aid training programme in anticipation of violence during and after the November 18 elections.
- A leading elections monitoring group, the Zambia Independent Monitoring Team, said it may refuse to monitor the November 18 polls because it does not want to legitimise a faulty electoral system.
